records.name: Youth Capital Academy
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit started in 2025 that teaches kids and teens money skills, business building, and leadership. It has worked with high schools and held a youth business fair.
records.what_you_do: Young people learn money skills, entrepreneurship and leadership through hands-on lessons and mentoring. The group reports helping more than 15 young people start businesses in 2025. Youth and families can use the Enroll Now form on the group's site, or email to ask about enrollment.

schedule.text: Programs meet one to two days a week, for about one to two hours a session, as workshops or multi-week series. Purpose to Profit is a 14-week program.

cost.text: Programs are free, and meals and snacks are provided. Selected Purpose to Profit students may receive up to $500 in startup funding.

first_step.how: Click Enroll Now on youthcapitalacademy.org to open the enrollment form, or email info@youthcapitalacademy.org to ask about times and places.
first_step.basis: Anyone can use the public enrollment form, but the site says spots are limited and does not say how they are filled.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sessions are hands-on, with games, mentoring and business-building activities, and meals and snacks are served. Most programs meet one to two days a week for one to two hours at a time, and Purpose to Profit runs for 14 weeks. The site does not list meeting places or times, so ask before the first session.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the enrollment form early, since spots are limited.
Ask about times and the meeting place by email before you come.
Youth Diversion sessions take youth referred by schools, community groups or justice partners, so ask whether a referral is needed.

records.notes: Ages 8 to 23 across the four programs. Youth Diversion is for ages 10 to 18 and takes youth referred by schools, community groups or justice partners. The programs page age line for Empowerment is hard to read, so 8 is the low end as the page gives it. court_ordered_ok and service_hours_letter stay unknown: the site mentions completion certificates for diversion, not service hours letters. Meeting places, times and group sizes are not published. The tier 1 contact form wording was replaced by the Enroll Now form, which the site shows.

records.name: African American Genealogy Group
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps people trace African American family history. It holds free public meetings with a speaker most months, and members can also join members-only workshops and interest group meetings.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free general meeting on the second Tuesday of the month, except July and August. The social hour is at 6 pm and the talk starts at 6:30 pm. The meeting is on Zoom, so register on the group's site to get the link. Membership is optional and unlocks members-only workshops.

schedule.text: General meetings on the second Tuesday of the month, except July and August. Social hour at 6 pm, talk at 6:30 pm.

cost.text: Meetings are free. Membership is optional: yearly dues are $25 (student, 26 and under), $40 (regular) or $75 (family), or $500 once for lifetime membership.

first_step.how: Register for the next monthly meeting on the group's registration page to get the Zoom link, then join for the 6 pm social hour or the 6:30 pm talk.
first_step.basis: The October 2026 talk is titled Beginning Your Genealogy, the page calls it a free event that welcomes visitors, and it links to a registration page. Other monthly talks are not described for beginners.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings are free and held on Zoom, so you can join from home after you register. A social hour starts at 6 pm and the speaker talk starts at 6:30 pm. The October 2026 talk covers genealogy tools and techniques, with some attention to Southern and African American records.
first_visit_tips: Register ahead on the group's site to get the Zoom link.
Members-only workshops need a membership; the monthly talk is open to visitors.
Joining online is immediate, while a mailed membership form takes 5 to 7 business days.

records.notes: Website set to https://aagg.org. The www host returned a certificate name error in WebFetch, so the tier 1 www address was replaced. online_ok is true because the monthly meeting registration leads to a Zoom link for October 2026. newcomer_friendliness is 4 only because of the October 2026 talk titled for beginners; the monthly talks in general are not described as beginner friendly, so this rating deserves a second look. Accessibility and languages are not stated on the pages read.

records.name: Anointed to Serve Ministries
records.summary: Helps older adults stay safe and independent at home with personal help, connections to services, and protection from exploitation.
records.what_you_do: Older adults and family members can ask about help at home, such as home repairs and utilities, technology and online government forms, basic legal and money guidance, and referrals to screened contractors. In-home support is free for seniors. The contact form is the way to ask.

cost.text: In-home support is free for seniors. Fees for other services are not stated.

first_step.how: Send a question through the Questions or Comments form on anointed2serve.org, or email info@anointed2serve.org, and ask what help is available for an older adult.
first_step.basis: The site lists services and a contact form but no intake steps, fees, or hours, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Your first step is a message through the contact form or by email. The group describes in-home help that comes to the person's home, plus help with paperwork, technology and home repairs. The site does not say how long a visit takes, when the office is open, or what other services cost.
first_visit_tips: The contact form asks for a name and email; a message is optional.
The form needs JavaScript turned on in your browser.
Ask about fees for services other than in-home support, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: Email changed from Katrina@anointedtoserve.org to info@anointed2serve.org, because the group's own pages list info@ and sponsors@ at anointed2serve.org and do not show the old address. The contact name Katrina Williams is also not on the site; the site names Dr. Katrina Polk as co-founder and board president and Sheree Davis as executive director. The name is kept pending a check. A staff bio mentions D.C. operations, so the service area is unclear. The site lists no hours or intake steps and does not state accessibility or languages.

records.name: Community Enrichment Fitness Network
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps older adults eat well and stay active through health events, nutrition programs, and a senior community where people meet and keep moving.
records.what_you_do: Come to health and nutrition events, join the senior community to socialize and stay active, or volunteer at events. Event volunteers help as greeters, ushers, parking attendants and in other roles.

schedule.text: Health and nutrition programs and events. A senior gala runs each spring and a harvest ball each fall.

cost.text: Prices for programs and events are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Call (215) 858-4957 or email cefnphila@gmail.com to ask how to join the next senior program or event, since the programs page lists no sign-up steps.
first_step.basis: Programs and events are for older adults, but the site gives no sign-up steps or ticket details, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events include live music, a DJ, catered food, health and wellness vendors and a raffle. The yearly fall ball has a dress code of elegant evening wear. Programs include nutrition and healthy cooking and a seated exercise class. The site does not list times, places or prices, so call before you come.
first_visit_tips: Ask about the venue, start time and ticket price before you come, since the site does not list them.
Volunteers attend a short briefing before each event starts.
To help out, use the interest form on the volunteer page, or call or email the group.

records.notes: The 6th Annual Senior Harvest Ball (Friday, October 23, 2026) is a one-time event, so it is out of schedule and cost and appears only as last_sign_of_life. The events page gives 9 am to 3 pm for the ball, while the homepage read as an evening event; that time is not recorded. The programs page has no sign-up steps; the homepage mentions a Join Us link, but its target was not read. newcomer_friendliness moved from 3 to 2 for that reason. The partners page names many corporate sponsors (insurers, drug companies, banks, home care firms); only Temple OLLI is listed as a lead.

records.name: Extended Play
records.summary: A nonprofit that works with filmmakers who make films for social change, handling grant money for film projects and helping arrange screenings and outreach in the Philadelphia area.
records.what_you_do: Email the group about a film project you are making. It can handle project funds through fiscal sponsorship and help set up screenings and distribution.

cost.text: Fiscal sponsorship takes a fee of 5% to 10% of the grant, depending on its size

first_step.how: Email extendedplayinc@gmail.com with a short description of your socially conscious film and what you need: funding, screenings, or distribution.
first_step.basis: The only way in is an email, and the site does not say how projects are chosen.
first_step.what_to_expect: This is not a class or a drop-in group. You send an email about a socially conscious film project and say whether you need funding, screenings or distribution. The site does not say how projects are chosen or how quickly the group replies, and fiscal sponsorship takes 5% to 10% of a grant.
first_visit_tips: Have a few lines ready about your film's goal, its stage, and the help you need.
Ask about the fiscal sponsorship fee before you commit, since it takes 5% to 10% of a grant.
The past projects page shows the kinds of films the group has backed from 2020 to 2025.

records.notes: The about page says the group's current focus began in 2026 but gives no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out and status stays probably_active. The past projects page covers 2020 to 2025 and gives only one year, 2024, for a festival trip; it is not used for status. The IPMF grant source and the SIFT program named on the past projects page are not added as leads; the page does not say enough to identify them.

records.name: Gathering Place
records.summary: A Philadelphia community space that brings people with different views together for conversation, creative arts, and small dinners.
records.what_you_do: Apply for a Set The Table dinner. Submissions are reviewed, about ten guests are picked to mix viewpoints, and chosen guests pay a $10 reservation fee. You can also put your email on the list for a Set The Table event to hear about it.

schedule.text: The dates for Set The Table dinners are listed as to be announced. The site gives no dates for its other sections.

cost.text: Chosen Set The Table guests pay a $10 reservation fee. Other event costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Submit your email under the Set The Table dinner you want on the group's Set The Table page. Submissions are reviewed, and about ten guests are chosen.
first_step.basis: Dinner seats are chosen from submissions, so the way in is an application; the event mailing list is open to anyone who sends an email.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Set The Table dinner brings about ten strangers with different views together to talk about hard topics such as politics, religion and race. Questions are asked anonymously at the table, and at the end people may choose to reveal who asked them. Dates are not yet set, and the dinner length and place are not stated before you apply.
first_visit_tips: If you are chosen, expect a $10 reservation fee; the group says it helps make sure guests attend.
The exact address is not published online, so call 267-538-1417 to ask where events are held.
Each event has its own mailing list, so sign up under the event you want.

records.notes: Open mic and paint night claims from tier 1 do not appear on the home, Set The Table, past events or media pages, and one web search found no listing. They are removed from summary, what_you_do and schedule, and the painting, storytelling and theater interests and families are removed with them. The home page still describes creative arts in general. Status moved from probably_active to dormant: the newest dated item is a June 2023 past event, and the Set The Table dinner dates are only listed as TBA. Please review this before publishing. The exact address is not published on the site (it lists Germantown, PA 19144), so the IRS address is kept as the mailing address. Sections TRIBE, MEN and DOZ are named on the site without descriptions and were not checked as separate groups.
